title: Hacker Runs Hermes AI Agent Unattended for Post-Exploitation at Thai Finance Ministry

reading.body:
An autonomous AI agent called Hermes was deployed by an attacker against Thailand's Ministry of Finance in July 2026 to conduct post-exploitation activities across the compromised network. The agent operated in unattended mode without human approval, automating attacks against Hadoop infrastructure, mail systems, GlassFish servers, and administrative panels. This represents a failure to detect and stop an AI system being used as an attack tool once the initial network compromise had occurred.

The attackers had already obtained stolen credentials and knowledge of internal network topology before deploying Hermes, suggesting the agent was used to scale reconnaissance and lateral movement across systems that had been previously identified. Catching this would have required network monitoring to identify the automated agent's behavior patterns, endpoint detection of the custom scripts and implants being deployed, or access controls preventing the use of harvested credentials at scale. The operation remained undetected for approximately five days until researchers found exposed attack infrastructure on a Hong Kong server.

It is not established whether the Hermes agent was a custom tool built by the attackers, an off-the-shelf system repurposed for attack, or the specific technical capabilities it possessed beyond what the custom scripts accomplished.

summary:
# Summary

Thailand's Ministry of Finance was targeted in a cyberattack from July 9-13, 2026, involving an autonomous AI agent called Hermes and a custom implant named Hades. Researchers at Hunt.io discovered three exposed directories on a Hong Kong server containing 585 files, 470 MB of attack code, stolen credentials, and logs showing the agent operating in unattended mode without human approval. The attackers deployed custom scripts targeting the ministry's Hadoop infrastructure, mail systems, GlassFish servers, and administrative panels, using hardcoded stolen credentials and multiple privilege escalation exploits.

The operation revealed sophisticated reconnaissance of Thailand's finance ministry network, including knowledge of internal hostnames and addresses. The attackers used purpose-built tools to exploit Apache HiveServer2, deploy web shells, and access mailbox systems. Evidence suggests initial compromise occurred in mid-to-late June 2026. Thailand's national cybersecurity authorities were notified on July 15, 2026, following a standard seven-day disclosure period before public release of the research.
